findings.source_passage: pushed her on like giants' palms outspread… sky and air seemed vast outbellying sails; the whole world boomed before the wind. Muffled in the full morning light, the invisible sun was only known by the spread intensity of his place; where his bayonet rays moved on in stacks. Emblazonings, as of crowned Babylonian kings and queens, reigned over everything.
findings.why_it_matters: The opening paragraph is a sustained piece of visionary prose—'giants' palms outspread,' 'bayonet rays moved on in stacks,' 'Emblazonings, as of crowned Babylonian kings and queens'—with distinctive prosodic and rhetorical weight that sets the apocalyptic register for the whole chapter. The draft retains only the 'outbellying sails' and 'boomed before the wind' phrases and strips the rest, erasing the chapter's signature opening voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum 'Emblazonings, as of crowned Babylonian kings and queens, reigned over everything' and either the 'bayonet rays' or 'giants' palms' image; these are the textually distinctive, interpretively weighted phrases that define the chapter's opening atmosphere.

findings.source_passage: "Ha, ha, my ship! thou mightest well be taken now for the sea-chariot of the sun. Ho, ho! all ye nations before my prow, I bring the sun to ye! Yoke on the further billows; hallo! a tandem, I drive the sea!"
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the chapter's primary set-pieces: Ahab's ecstatic, rhythmically distinctive speech in which he identifies himself with the sun-chariot. The draft drops 'thou mightest well be taken now for the sea-chariot of the sun,' 'Yoke on the further billows,' and 'I drive the sea!'—the most memorable and interpretively important phrases—retaining only a fragment of the middle line.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full speech verbatim or near-verbatim; at minimum preserve 'sea-chariot of the sun' and 'I drive the sea!' as these carry interpretive weight about Ahab's solar megalomania.

findings.source_passage: "Thou poor, proud heaven-gazer and sun's pilot! yesterday I wrecked thee, and to-day the compasses would fain have wrecked me. So, so. But Ahab is lord over the level loadstone yet."
findings.source_locator: paragraph after 'chancing to slip with his ivory heel'
findings.why_it_matters: Ahab's address to the broken quadrant—'Thou poor, proud heaven-gazer and sun's pilot!'—is a critically noted apostrophe connecting this chapter to the preceding one and encapsulating the theme of instruments that fail or are made to submit. The entire speech is absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore this apostrophe; it is the thematic hinge between the quadrant chapter and this one, and 'heaven-gazer and sun's pilot' is a signature phrase.

findings.source_passage: their fear of Ahab was greater than their fear of Fate. But as ever before, the pagan harpooneers remained almost wholly unimpressed; or if impressed, it was only with a certain magnetism shot into their congenial hearts from inflexible Ahab's.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Meanwhile, whatever were his own secret thoughts'
findings.why_it_matters: The contrast between the crew's fear of Ahab vs. Fate, and the singular note about the harpooneers receiving 'a certain magnetism' from Ahab, is both interpretively weighted (the magnetism pun is thematically integral) and voice-distinctive. The draft omits the entire Starbuck/Stubb/Flask/crew response paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence preserving at minimum 'their fear of Ahab was greater than their fear of Fate' and the magnetism image for the harpooneers.

findings.source_passage: Abashed glances of servile wonder were exchanged by the sailors… But Starbuck looked away.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Ahab's 'my men, the thunder turned' speech
findings.why_it_matters: 'But Starbuck looked away' is a three-word stroke of great interpretive power—Starbuck's moral withdrawal from Ahab's theatre of mastery. Its absence erases a key character beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'But Starbuck looked away' verbatim; it requires only four words and its omission is a significant character and interpretive loss.

findings.source_passage: whether indispensable to the magnetizing of the steel, or merely intended to augment the awe of the crew, is uncertain
findings.why_it_matters: This parenthetical is a characteristic Melvillean ironic aside that keeps deliberate interpretive ambiguity about Ahab's sincerity vs. performance alive—a narratorial voice moment that the compression has silently dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical doubt ('whether indispensable… or merely intended to augment the awe… is uncertain') as it carries the chapter's characteristic ironic undercurrent.

summary: The draft commits three high-severity signature losses—the visionary opening ('Emblazonings…crowned Babylonian kings,' 'bayonet rays'), Ahab's sea-chariot speech, and his apostrophe to the broken quadrant—plus three medium losses including 'But Starbuck looked away' and the fear-of-Ahab-vs.-Fate passage, collectively gutting the chapter's rhetoric, thematic architecture, and voice.
